M29 live buffered playback.Source: P-A2: in live real mode the server's producer thread steps the engine into a frame buffer and the screens play from it; playback never passes the newest computed minute, so if the engine is slower than 1x (diag-11 v2 on the 3060 desktop: up to 106.9 s for 1441 steps against 105 s of playback) playback slows to the engine's pace and the screens hold the newest frame instead of jumping. The producer leads by at most the head start plus 2 minutes. Off: the old inline stepping on the event loop. Fake mode never buffers.

M29 live playback head start seconds.Source: P-A2 (design call, Nov 4; may be raised later): seconds of 1x playback buffered before the screens start, and with 2 minutes the most the engine runs ahead. diag-11 sized a fixed-rate head start at 12 s (max(0, 106.9 - 105) + 10); with playback clamped to the newest computed minute it only has to absorb step jitter, and a smaller lead means a mid-run post (the insured chip) takes effect about 2 s after the minute on screen (27 simulated minutes at 1441/105 per second) instead of about 12 s (165 minutes). Raise it if diag-04 live_smoke --server shows stutter.
